title: Unit 1 Quiz · Introduction to Predictive Analytics
instructions: 33 questions, 37 marks. You have 30 minutes; the quiz submits itself when time runs out.
Questions and options are shuffled, so your neighbour's screen will not match yours.
Multi-select questions need ALL correct options for the marks. Ordering questions give part marks for each item in the right place.
After submitting you will see your score and an explanation for every question.

questions.q: Which statement best describes predictive analytics?
options: Using historical data, statistics and machine learning to estimate the probability of future or unknown outcomes, to support decisions
Making charts of last month’s sales
Storing large amounts of customer data safely
Guaranteeing what will happen in the future
questions.explain: Predictive analytics learns from past cases with known outcomes and gives a probability for new cases. It never guarantees the future.

questions.q: In a churn model, the column “churned” (Yes/No) is the:
questions.explain: The target is the outcome we want to predict. Tenure, support calls and plan type are predictors.

questions.q: A model gives a customer a churn probability of 0.70. What does this mean?
options: Among customers like this one, about 70 in 100 are expected to leave
questions.explain: A probability describes the risk for customers similar to this one. It is not certain, and it is not the model’s accuracy.

questions.q: Which type of analytics answers “What should we do?”
questions.explain: Prescriptive analytics recommends an action, combining predictions with costs, benefits and constraints.

questions.q: A report says “22.7% of customers left last quarter.” Which type of analytics is this?
questions.explain: It summarises what already happened: descriptive.

questions.q: Analysts find that leavers made more support calls than stayers, to explain why customers left. This is:
questions.explain: Explaining why something happened is diagnostic analytics.

questions.q: Arrange the types of analytics from LEAST to MOST valuable (and difficult).
questions.explain: Descriptive → Diagnostic → Predictive → Prescriptive: from hindsight to foresight to action.

questions.q: A maps app choosing the fastest route for you, given live traffic, is mainly:
questions.explain: Estimating travel time is predictive; choosing the best route for you is a recommended action: prescriptive.

questions.q: 340 of 1,500 customers churned. What is the churn rate?
A trend line gives revenue = 482.81 + 5.664 × t (₹ lakh), with t = 1 for Jan 2023. What is the forecast for t = 25?
For t = 1 to 5 the fitted line is ŷ = 8.7 + 1.5 t. What is the forecast for t = 6?
A logistic model uses p = 1 / (1 + e^(−z)). What is p when z = 0?
questions.explain: e⁰ = 1, so p = 1 / (1 + 1) = 0.5. Positive z gives p above 0.5; negative z gives p below 0.5.

questions.q: Only 22.7% of customers churn. What accuracy does a lazy model that always predicts “No” get?
questions.explain: It is right for every customer who stays: 100% − 22.7% = 77.3%. That is why accuracy alone can be misleading.

questions.q: The 10% of customers a model rates riskiest churn at 48.9%; the overall churn rate is 22.7%. What is the lift?
questions.explain: Lift = 48.9 ÷ 22.7 ≈ 2.16: the top group contains about twice as many leavers as a random group.

questions.q: Expected gain = p × 0.40 × ₹2,000 − ₹300. What is the expected gain when p = 0.5?
questions.explain: 0.5 × 0.40 × 2,000 = 400; 400 − 300 = +₹100, so the offer is worth making.

questions.q: Select ALL of the following that are predictive analytics applications.
options: Predicting machine failure from sensor readings
Forecasting next month’s demand for each product
questions.explain: The first three estimate unknown or future outcomes. Printing payslips is routine processing, not analytics.

questions.q: In manufacturing, predictive maintenance mainly predicts:
options: Which machine is likely to fail soon, so it can be serviced first
How many workers joined last year
The price of raw material last month
Which product sold most last year
questions.explain: Sensor data (vibration, temperature) is used to predict failures before they happen.

questions.q: Customer reviews, call recordings and photos are examples of:
questions.explain: They have no predefined rows and columns, so they are unstructured.

questions.q: JSON data sent by a mobile app is usually:
questions.explain: JSON has keys and tags, but no fixed table layout: semi-structured.

questions.q: The number of support calls (0, 1, 2, …) is:
questions.explain: It is a count of whole numbers, so it is discrete quantitative data.

questions.q: Monthly revenue of one company for 24 months in a row is:
questions.explain: One subject measured over time is a time series. Many subjects at one time is cross-sectional; many subjects over time is panel data.

questions.q: Customer satisfaction recorded as 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 is measured on which scale?
questions.explain: The values have an order, but the gaps between them are not guaranteed equal: ordinal.

questions.q: Temperature in °C is measured on which scale?
questions.explain: Equal gaps, but 0 °C is not “no temperature”: interval.

questions.q: Monthly charge in rupees is measured on which scale?
questions.explain: ₹0 means no money (a true zero), so ratios make sense: ₹800 is twice ₹400. Ratio.

questions.q: Which summary is valid for a NOMINAL variable such as plan type?
questions.explain: Nominal values are only labels, so you can count them and find the most common one. A mean of plan types has no meaning.

questions.q: In SPSS Variable View, interval and ratio variables are both given which Measure?
questions.explain: SPSS combines interval and ratio into “Scale”. (Numeric is a Type, not a Measure.)

questions.q: Why is 40 °C NOT “twice as hot” as 20 °C?
options: The Celsius scale has no true zero
questions.explain: Ratios need a true zero. 0 °C is just the freezing point of water, not an absence of heat.

questions.q: Arrange the stages of the predictive analytics lifecycle in order.
questions.explain: Define → Collect → Prepare → Explore → Build → Evaluate → Deploy → Monitor, then repeat.

questions.q: Why is a model evaluated on a test set it has never seen?
options: To get an honest estimate of how it will perform on new customers
Because test data is always cleaner
Because the training data is deleted after training
questions.explain: A model can memorise its training data. Unseen data shows how it will really perform after deployment.

questions.q: A deployed churn model gets less accurate over months because customer behaviour changes. This is called:
questions.explain: Model drift is why the lifecycle ends with monitoring and retraining, then starts again.

questions.q: Which Excel function makes a straight-line forecast?
questions.explain: =FORECAST.LINEAR(x, known_y, known_x) uses the least-squares trend line.

questions.q: Which tool is a free, open-source language built mainly for statistics?
questions.explain: R was created by statisticians and is free. Excel and SPSS are paid products.

questions.q: In R, which call fits a logistic regression for a Yes/No target?
questions.explain: glm with family = binomial fits logistic regression. lm fits a straight line, as used for the revenue trend.
